title: UML: use case, class, sequence, component and deployment diagrams

videos.script: UML has fourteen kinds of diagram. Most working architects use five of them, and that is what this lesson teaches. {{title}} Each one answers a different question about the same system. {{five}} A use case diagram says who does what with the system, and where the system ends. {{usecase}} A class diagram says which things exist and how they relate. Here it draws one aggregate from the design patterns course. {{class}} A sequence diagram puts time on the page. Messages go down the screen, one after another, and you can count the waits. {{sequence}} A component diagram shows what each part offers and what it needs. {{component}} And a deployment diagram says where it all runs. {{deployment}} The notation is strict in small places. A diamond on the wrong end reverses the meaning. So for each diagram you will see it right, and then wrong.
